correctness.rationale: A unital endomorphism is a freely chosen triple of cube-zero elements in the maximal ideal. Outside characteristic three the surviving x_i²x_j coefficients force at most one nonzero linear coordinate per image. With that coordinate x and a=v+xu+x²w, u is a unit; the x-equation gives v²=0, and then the x²-equation gives vu²=0, hence v=0. This uses both equations, not the assertion that a square-zero element vanishes. For zero linear part, only the cube of the quadratic part matters and its socle coefficient is 3(2ABC+2DEF+AF²+BE²+CD²), with 17 free higher coefficients. In char. 2, the equation is linear in A,B,C with a single exceptional zero triple (D,E,F). In other non-3 characteristics solving for C gives q² exceptional (A,B,D); among them the zero triple contributes q² pairs, 2(q−1) rank-one triples q each, and (q−1)² nondegenerate binary forms contribute q+(q−1)χ_q(6) each since −det=(3/2)D². This yields the printed Z_q over the actual field. Occupied coordinate directions give rank, hence the stated inclusion–exclusion formulas. In char. 3 all maximal-ideal images work by Frobenius with 23 free coefficients for each column and the usual matrix-rank count. The nonpolynomial dependence is genuine: along even and odd powers of 7 the two different character signs give different polynomial expressions for the singular census, each on infinitely many field sizes.
residual_risks: No uploaded script was executed. The finite checks do not cover odd-prime extensions, which are covered by the binary quadratic-form proof. The phrase 'rank-at-most-one obstruction' describes single columns, not a bound on the rank of the whole endomorphism.
